Below is a practical plan you can execute on your own workstation (the sandbox can’t really “move” a file into a sub‑folder because the `mv`/`cp` helpers forbid paths).

---

## 1. Put both reports together

Assuming your project layout looks like this before anything else runs:

```
project/
├─ document/
│  ├─ final_report.pdf
│  └─ previous_report.pdf
└─ …
```

Create the temporary holding area and copy/move the PDFs there:

```sh
cd document                # switch to the folder that holds the PDFs
mkdir -p temp              # create the helper folder

# Move the old report into temp
mv previous_report.pdf temp/

# Move the new report into temp
mv final_report.pdf    temp/
```

Afterwards you’ll see:

```
project/
└─ document/
   └─ temp/
      ├─ previous_report.pdf
      └─ final_report.pdf
```

*(In the sandbox you can mimic this by staying in `/workspace/document` and issuing the commands shown above—the `mv` calls work fine once you’re in the right directory.)*

---

## 2. Turn each PDF into plain text

A PDF is a complex binary structure; most comparison tools expect plain text. On Linux/macOS you can use `pdftotext` (part of Poppler) or `xpdf`.

```sh
# Install poppler utils if needed:
sudo apt-get install poppler-utils          # Debian/Ubuntu
brew install poppler                         # macOS Homebrew

# Convert both PDFs
pdftotext temp/previous_report.pdf prev.txt
pdftotext temp/final_report.pdf     fin.txt
```

Resulting files (`prev.txt`, `fin.txt`) now hold the textual representation of each report.

---

## 3. Identify “critical alterations”

There are several ways to surface meaningful differences:

| Method | How it helps | Example command |
|--------|---------------|------------------|
| **Line‑by‑line diff** | Shows added/deleted lines exactly | `diff --color=always -u prev.txt fin.txt` |
| **Word‑level diff** | Highlights changed phrases even if surrounding context stays | `sdiff -s prev.txt fin.txt` |
| **Semantic diff** | Detects structural changes (sections, tables) | Run a script that parses headers (`=== Budget ===`) and compares blockwise. |
| **Keyword focus** | Pull out only parts mentioning key terms (“budget”, “forecast”) | `grep -i -C3 -n \"budget\" fin.txt > fin_budgets.txt` |

For a quick visual scan, the classic unified diff usually suffices:

```sh
diff --color=always -u prev.txt fin.txt | less -R
```

Lines prefixed with `+` were inserted in the new version; `–` marks deletions. Pay special attention to:

* Sections renamed or removed.
* Numerical values that differ significantly (especially budgets, forecasts).
* New warnings or footnotes that weren’t present before.

---

## 4. Optional: Highlight only “budget analysis” changes

If you specifically want to spot modifications around the *budget analysis* section, filter the diffs:

```sh
# Grab the whole “Budget Analysis” block from each file
awk '
  /^==\s*Budget\sAnalysis\s*=*/{flag=1}
  flag && !/^==/{print}
  /^==[^=]/ {if(flag){exit}}
' prev.txt > prev_budget.txt

awk '
  /^==\s*Budget\sAnalysis\s*=*/{flag=1}
  flag && !/^==/{print}
  /^==[^=]/ {if(flag){exit}}
' fin.txt > fin_budget.txt

# Diff those blocks
diff --color=always -u prev_budget.txt fin_budget.txt | less -R
```

This isolates the exact paragraph(s)/table(s) dealing with budgeting so you don’t waste time scrolling through unrelated material.

---

## 5. Summarize findings

Once you’ve inspected the diff output, jot down the key points:

| Item | Old value | New value | Impact |
|------|-----------|----------|-------|
| Total operating cost | $1,200k | $1,350k | +13% increase |
| Marketing spend | $300k | $250k | Decrease |
| Forecasted revenue | $5M | $4.8M | Slight dip |

These bullet points give stakeholders a concise snapshot of what truly changed.

---

### Bottom line

Because the sandbox’s file utilities restrict cross‑folder moves, you’ll need to carry out the actual relocation and conversion on your local machine. Once you have the plaintext versions, standard UNIX diff tools will expose every alteration—including subtle ones—in the “budget analysis” section and elsewhere.
